result.reason: Clarity: A orders the material the way a reader expects (performance, then positioning, then fee change, then disclosure), while B buries the quarterly return until its fourth paragraph. A glosses jargon for a non-specialist ("gross of fees, that is, before the advisory fee was deducted"; explains why not selling equities matters) and uses explicit First/Second/Third signposting; B leaves "gross-of-fees," "strategic parameters," and "five-point band" unexplained, omits the 25% fixed income target so the reader cannot judge whether 27.5% is significant, joins unrelated points with "Similarly," and contains a garbled clause ("Treasury securities taken advantage of during recent yield spikes"). Tone: the notes call for a formal board letter to be read into the April 28 minutes. A has full letterhead and date, addresses the chair and the board, sustains a neutral fiduciary register, and closes by referencing the April 28 meeting and offering to take questions. B lacks letterhead, date, and any reference to the board or meeting, addresses only the chair, and tips into promotion during a negative quarter ("our team successfully executed," "compares favorably," "remains strong," "We are pleased to inform you" of a fee change); it also adopts the foundation's 5% payout obligation as "our target," misplacing whose duty it is. A wins on structure and register rather than length; both letters are comparable in length.
